subject: Promptset regression: coordinated mitigation plan and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Park <joe.park@acme-consulting.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

Hi Priyom,

We started a small A/B lift on our shopping guidance flow using promptset-v3 (your team’s new prompt suite) and we’re seeing a measurable regression in helpfulness for a subset of queries — roughly 8% drop in NDCG on our internal eval. I’m attaching the raw eval run (eval-run-20270311.csv).

Can we pause the rollout in the next few hours and get a short cross-functional sync? We need:
- a quick triage to determine whether this is a prompt failure or an artifact of the model variant
- a temporary fallback policy for live traffic if needed
- a concrete acceptance criteria to lift the pause

Thanks,
Elena
Product Lead, Search & Discovery
Stellar Retail
[attachment: eval-run-20270311.csv]
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

Elena — thanks for the flag and the data. I’ll pull the team together. Initial asks: can you share the traffic slice (user cohorts) and the HubSpot record for the rollout? Joe/ACME, appreciate any quick CI logs you can surface.

Immediate plan (we should confirm on a call):
1) Pause canary: switch routing back to promptset-v2 for the 20% cohort.
2) Re-run the eval with the exact live prompts and prefixes recorded in logs (we’ll use promptset-v3 with the same input distribution).
3) Define acceptance gates for relaunch (see suggested criteria below).

Suggested acceptance criteria (first pass):
- No more than 2% negative delta in NDCG on the production prompt slice measured across the last 7 days.
- No statistically significant increase in hallucination rate measured by the existing hallucination annotator (p < 0.05).
- No regression on top-5 intent accuracy for our priority vertical (electronics/home).

I’m scheduling a 30-min triage at 11:00 PT. Markus — can you attend and own runtime checks? Lauren — can you own eval/annotator re-runs? Marissa — can you take notes and own the rollout change? Karthik — I want a quick read on the prompt delta and possible fallback short-term edits.

—Priyom
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
[attachment: mutual_action_plan.md]
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

I’ll be there. Quick notes from infra side: latency and token distribution for the canary cohort look unchanged; no GPU OOMs or retries. I’m going to snapshot the canary traffic routing config before we flip, and I’ll enable a 1x higher sampling of KV cache hits for deeper inspection.

If we do a rollback to promptset-v2 for the 20% as Priyom suggested, I’ll coordinate the routing change and the rollback playbook (including monitoring alarms).

-Markus
Senior Infra Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

I’ll re-run the eval with the exact live inputs. Two quick asks for Elena:
1) Can you confirm which request logs correspond to the 20% canary window (time range + trace IDs if available)?
2) Do you have any manual annotations from customer support that align with the drop?

Plan for the triage call:
- Reproduce eval locally (Lauren)
- Check prompt diffs and tokenization (Karthik)
- Check runtime anomalies (Markus)
- Decide rollback/fallback thresholds (Priyom/Elena)

I’ll attach the promptset-v3 bundle and the re-run steps to the Drive link afterwards.

-Lauren
Lead Eval Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: promptset-v3.json]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

Quick note from prompt analysis: I compared promptset-v2 vs v3 diffs — there are three re-orderings and one new system-level instruction that will tighten summarization. That could surface as lower helpfulness for open-ended guidance queries. I’ll prototype a targeted edit (remove the tightening instruction for the discovery vertical) and push a test patch to the eval harness; should have results in ~45m.

-Karthik
Applied ML, Prompting
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

Summary from the 11:00 triage call:
- We flipped routing for the 20% canary back to promptset-v2. Markus completed the routing snapshot.
- Lauren reproduced the negative delta locally on the live slice and confirmed the annotator flagged higher hallucination in open-ended queries.
- Karthik’s quick patch removing the tightening instruction improves helpfulness in the discovery slice by ~3.5% in the re-run (prelim).
- Action items:
  * Karthik: finalize the targeted prompt edit and push to a staging variant (due EOD 3/12).
  * Lauren: run full re-annotation on the 3/12 re-run and surface precision recall metrics (due 3/13).
  * Marissa: coordinate a controlled relaunch plan and change log; include rollback hooks (due 3/13).
  * Markus: keep enhanced sampling on for 48h and escalate any infra anomalies.

Elena — if the 3/13 re-run looks clean against the acceptance criteria I posted earlier, are you comfortable with a staged relaunch (10% -> 40% -> 100%) with 2-hour observation windows?

—Priyom
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stellar-retail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Joe Park <joe.park@acme-consulting.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected regressions in promptset-v3 A/B

Thanks team — update from our side: the 3/13 re-run looks much better. Lauren’s annotator results show the hallucination rate back within baseline (1.1% delta) and the NDCG delta is +0.4% (within the 2% tolerance). We’re happy to proceed with the staged relaunch Priyom suggested, but please keep the rollback hook tight — we’ll also keep our CS monitoring on higher sampling for the next 72 hours.

I’ll follow up with an executive note to our stakeholders once the 40% window is stable. Good coordination — appreciate the quick response.

—Elena
Product Lead, Stellar Retail
